parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the benchmark as a cleanroom behavioral reimplementation of the provided binary, based only on normal CLI interaction and bundled documentation.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent spawned three focused probe children for help text, persistent state, and open/opdir/config behavior, while retaining responsibility for implementation, integration, compile, tests, and final answer.
parallel.implementation: The parent implemented a Rust crate with Cargo.toml, compile.sh, src/main.rs, and state modules after combining its own probes with child findings about CLI, state, move/vmove, config, and open behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent alone wrote the final source tree and installed the compiled replacement as ./executable; child outputs were informational and did not create competing implementation artifacts.
parallel.verification: The parent compiled repeatedly, ran side-by-side checks and smoke tests, then ran compile.sh and checked the installed executable before final delivery.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed 53 of 846 tests, and the final response identified vault listing order as residual uncertainty; hidden behavior remained unmatched.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same cleanroom task and reverse-engineered by running the binary and reading bundled docs without delegation or external source lookup.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, integration, build, verification, cleanup, and final answer in one sequential workflow.
serial.implementation: After extensive sequential probing, the serial run wrote a Rust crate with Cargo.toml, compile.sh, src/main.rs, and state/config modules, then patched parser, HOME, remove, and panic-path details.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run installed the replacement as ./executable, removed its temporary xdg-open probe helper, cleaned the Cargo build output, and left source plus the executable in the submission.
serial.verification: It diff-checked help, config, list, vault, open, opdir, and several parser/runtime errors against the original, then performed post-install sanity checks.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed 201 of 846 tests, showing many hidden behavior mismatches despite the local diff checks and final sanity checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the need for a from-scratch executable matching observed CLI behavior and documented the allowed behavioral-probing approach.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same cleanroom constraints and used normal CLI interaction and bundled docs as the source of truth.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirements-level misunderstanding separates the outcomes; both understood the cleanroom task, but parallel covered more behavior in practice.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent delegated three behavioral probes but kept implementation, build, final integration, and delivery ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent performed all probing, implementation, build, and final checks itself without subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained focused concurrent behavioral discovery without losing owner accountability; serial traded that for a single sequential workflow.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The children were briefed for behavioral probing and returned summaries that were compatible with the parent's single implementation path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run retained all observed context internally and moved from probing to implementation after declaring the probe set sufficient.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced handoff boundaries, but they returned concise usable findings and did not create incompatible interfaces; serial avoided handoff risk by staying single-agent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent wrote the main Rust implementation after probing many command families and edge cases, then iterated through compile fixes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run waited longer before implementation, wrote a large Rust main file, and later split out a state/config module for panic-path fidelity.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both chose Rust and similar file layouts; parallel started implementation after combining concurrent probe outputs and produced a higher-scoring but still incomplete behavior model.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent experienced a routine wait timeout but later listed agents and received child findings; the child results were not trapped or ignored.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results; the single agent carried findings forward directly from probes into implementation and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra result lifecycle steps but no realized lifecycle failure; serial had no handoff lifecycle to manage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent alone wrote final implementation files, while a child cleaned accidental default-home jot state before returning; no competing source edits or consumed leaked artifacts are visible.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run created a temporary xdg-open helper for probing, used it for open/opdir, deleted it, and cleaned the build directory before final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both touched transient probe state, but neither shows a final shared-state collision; parallel's child cleanup is a near-match for contamination only, not a retained pattern.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent performed compile checks, source-side behavior comparisons, final compile.sh install, and a smoke test, while acknowledging residual vault order uncertainty.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run performed compile checks, repeated side-by-side diffs, mutation checks, post-install sanity checks, and a panic-path check.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified representative behavior locally; neither ran the hidden evaluator before closure, and both missed evaluator cases despite local success.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run completed within the budget after about 1361 agent seconds, with 3 spawned probes and final task completion.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run completed within the budget after about 1210 agent seconds, with no subagents and a final task completion.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more aggregate requests and time but finished with stronger official coverage; there is no evidence that fan-out exhausted the budget or displaced required implementation work.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current completed evaluations are not discordant: both submissions failed. Parallel passed 793 of 846 tests while serial passed 645 of 846, so the observable difference is degree of behavioral coverage rather than a pass/fail split. Parallel used child probes to map help, state, and open/config behavior while the parent continued probing and then implemented; serial performed similar work sequentially and still missed more hidden cases.
parallel_contributors: Spawned three focused probe children for help text, persistent state, and open/opdir/config behavior while the parent continued additional behavior probes.
Integrated a larger observed behavior surface into a Rust replacement and ran compile, comparison, and smoke checks before final delivery.
Still left hidden behavior mismatches, with the final response explicitly noting vault listing order uncertainty.
serial_contributors: Probed the CLI, state, move/remove/open/config behavior sequentially and then implemented one Rust replacement.
Ran many representative diffs and post-install checks but ended with more official failures than the parallel run.
Had no subagent coordination boundary, so its lower score is ordinary coverage or implementation shortfall rather than a concurrency effect.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both implementations were incomplete against hidden tests; the parallel implementation matched more of the evaluator surface.
The parallel final called out residual vault listing order uncertainty, and the serial final did not identify an equivalent unresolved ordering issue.
The serial run spent more of its single trajectory on sequential probing before implementation, while parallel overlapped several probe surfaces.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No official outcome discordance; supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause.

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly owned and performed implementation after probing, adding the Rust source tree itself; no implementation owner was missing.
The children produced probe summaries, not separate components requiring cross-agent integration; the parent integrated all behavior into one codebase.
The parent created compile.sh, built the replacement, installed ./executable, and delivered the final artifact.
The parent carried the end-to-end pipeline from probing through source creation, build, checks, and final response.
No single mandatory preflight gate blocked productive work; the parent kept probing and later implemented while child probe work was available.
The parallel run overlapped multiple investigations and still completed implementation and verification; investigation did not leave later work incomplete by deferral.
Implementation, build, and final checks received active parent capacity; no indispensable critical path was starved by auxiliary child probes.
The three-child fan-out completed within the run and did not exhaust the budget or prevent final implementation, build, and smoke tests.
Each child had a focused probe scope and returned a usable summary; no child was assigned an overbroad implementation task that remained unfinished.
The delegated work was probing, and the children produced usable findings; no known requirement omitted from a child brief made work unusable or forced rework.
No separately owned implementation components needed interoperation; children returned behavioral observations for a parent-owned implementation.
The child findings were returned as summaries; there is no evidence that a known finding disappeared in transfer and caused repeated or wrong work.
The returned summaries were long but decision-structured and used; no returned handoff was too bulky to consume before implementation.
No child handoff described superseded workspace or requirement state that the parent then consumed to make an invalid integration decision.
The child summaries did not present unresolved incompatible contracts or observations that blocked or corrupted integration.
The parent did run integrated compile and smoke checks before final delivery; hidden evaluator failures alone cannot establish this label.
There was no replacement or retry episode that lacked inherited findings and repeated prior failed work.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: No active child was explicitly stopped, cancelled, or interrupted before its needed result was finalized.
The parent promoted and installed the candidate executable before closure; no complete candidate was left unplaced or packaged too late.
There was no child implementation merge after verification; child outputs were probe summaries and parent verification followed implementation changes.
No child produced a delegated implementation that the parent failed to retrieve or merge.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding trapped below the parent before closure; the children returned probe summaries.
No required child failed or was cancelled in a way that left scope unreassigned; child probe work completed and the parent continued.
The completed child results were available and reflected in the parent's implementation and final behavior coverage, not ignored.
One wait timed out, but the parent listed agents, later received results, and continued productive probing and implementation without deadline harm.
No concurrent agents wrote competing implementation files or overlapping source designs; only the parent produced the final codebase.
There is no visible same-file edit by two live agents and no observed reconciliation of another agent's concurrent source change.
No actor replaced or deleted non-entry source created by another actor; implementation source was parent-owned.
The parent alone installed the final ./executable; no child owned or overwrote the deliverable.
No broad cleanup or promotion replaced another agent's final-tree work or invalidated provenance.
Although agents shared the task environment, there was no unstable implementation state or provenance problem from multiple live writers.
The open/config child briefly created default-home jot state and then deleted it; no other actor is shown consuming that artifact as stable input or reference behavior.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The routine wait timeout, later result receipt, and final verification form one harmless lifecycle near-match, not a retained Load Imbalance or Blind Timeout chain.
The temporary default-home state cleanup is a harmless shared-environment near-match, not Artifact Leakage because it was not consumed by another actor.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were considered; no visible parallel coordination event had a realized adverse consequence.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No labels were retained because the failures are better explained as ordinary incomplete behavioral reimplementation, not observable concurrency mistakes.
